messages:
support-jen: FYI customer (acct: acme-inc) reports a sudden increase in 5xxs and  latency — they say ~30% of requests are getting routed to eu-west and timing out. attaching their sample request/response.

support-jen: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX" -H "x-region-hint: na-east" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

support-jen: response body: `{
  "error": "service_unavailable",
  "message": "fallback to eu-west timed out"
}` (503)

matt-eng-sre: looking. do we have trace id from the customer? need a sample request id + time window. also checking queue metrics for na-east. @infra-bot can you dump queue-lengths for na-east for the 15m window starting 2026-06-01T14:10Z?

support-jen: trace_id=01H7ZQ9K0X8T3A1; sent at 2026-06-01T14:17:03Z.customer says this started roughly at 14:00 UTC and lasted ~20m.

infra-bot: alert: na-east serving-pool queue_length=1240, head_latency_p50=240ms, head_latency_p95=1.8s, spillover_rate=18% during 2026-06-01T14:00-14:20Z. Autospillover policy triggered to eu-west and na-west.

matt-eng-sre: confirmed — na-east hit the 85% capacity threshold and autospillover started. looks like many requests were forwarded to eu-west.

priya-ops: two notes: 1) customer has a region pin via org settings? if they pinned to na-east and token has restricted scopes, a cross-region fallback can fail auth and surface 401/403 instead of successful fallback. 2) If their token is fine, cross-region will still add 150-400ms network overhead + cold-starts in fallback pool.

support-jen: customer says they did NOT pin region, they expected automatic fallback. they saw increased billing and then some failed requests. liam, did billing show anything unusual?

liam-billing: yep we saw a short-term spike in inter-region egress billing for that account in that window + 7% higher token units due to retries. charging note sent to acct team.

emily-platform: adding some detail — our spillover path does two things: (A) try compatible model variant in fallback region, (B) if token has region constraint it attempts to mint cross-region session which can fail. when mint fails we currently return 503 with message "fallback failed". that's what customer hit.

support-jen: repro steps the customer provided (they reproduced in their staging):
1) set header `x-region-hint: na-east`
2) send 200 concurrent requests with prompt size ~250 tokens
3) observe ~18% routed to eu-west, some responses 503 with body `fallback failed` or long tails 2s+.

matt-eng-sre: thanks. quick checks for us: grab the trace id and run `GET /debug/trace/01H7ZQ9K0X8T3A1` to see routing decisions. also check auth service logs for region-constraint failures for that token.

support-jen: pasted trace dump:
routing: na-east -> overflow -> eu-west
decision: autospillover triggered (capacity 0.87)
auth-check: token_scope=global, token_issued_region=na-east, session_mint_attempt=cross-region, result=DENIED (policy:region_restrict)
outcome: fallback attempted, auth denied -> service returned 503

priya-ops: that matches. token_issued_region mismatch + org policy prevented session mint. we need to change fallback behavior to try an alternate flow: either (1) attempt read-only inference path that doesn't require session mint, or (2) surface a clearer 401 with explanation so customers can fix region pin/token scope.

matt-eng-sre: short-term mitigation — we can temporarily route acme-inc traffic to na-west which is underutilized and not require cross-region mint (na-west has warmed pools for this model). will open a manual pin for the account and notify support.

support-jen: customer agreed to temporary pin to na-west. applying manual override now.

infra-bot: action: manual_pin applied for acct acme-inc -> na-west until 2026-06-02T00:00Z by matt-eng-sre.

matt-eng-sre: long-term action items: (1) change autospillover to prefer warm fallback pools within same continent to reduce auth cross-region attempts; (2) improve error codes: return 401/403 when auth reasons block fallback and include `x-fallback-reason` header; (3) add guardrail to avoid retries that double-bill when fallback fails.

liam-billing: logging follow-up with finance to credit the obvious double-bill window; will loop in acct team.

support-jen: customer is happy with manual pin for now. marking as escalated -> resolved workaround. filing a ticket with prioritization for the autospill behavior changes. :white_check_mark:

matt-eng-sre: tagging @product for rollout discussion.

priya-ops: note for postmortem: include the queueing trigger thresholds, how token scope interacts with fallback, and the cost impact per account.

support-jen: thanks all. closing thread after followups documented in ticket: PLAT-9832.
